Garnish with fresh julienned ginger, thinly sliced red chilies, and finely chopped green onions. Add fresh cilantro sprigs. Serve immediately.
notes: Use a light lager for the beer to complement the delicate salmon and avoid overpowering the black bean sauce.
Adjust the amount of fresh red chilies to your preferred level of heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of Lamb Ragu with Pappardelle is served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Wide, al dente pappardelle ribbons are thoroughly coated in a deep, rich red-brown tomato and lamb ragu. Large, tender, shredded chunks of slow-braised lamb are visibly nestled throughout the sauce. The dish is topped with a generous mound of freshly grated pale yellow Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, with a small sprig of fresh green basil providing a vibrant color contrast. The overall presentation is hearty and rustic, yet refined, showcasing the rich textures and deep colors of the slow-cooked sauce and tender lamb. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table, accompanied by traditional Italian flatware and a folded cotton napkin, creating an inviting and authentic casual dining scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the rich sauce.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil or parsley, for garnish

instructions: Cut lamb shoulder into 3-4 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb chunks in batches until well browned on all sides. Remove lamb from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, chopped rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Return seared lamb to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well to combine.
Bring the ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot.
Simmer for 2.5-3 hours, or until the lamb is very tender and easily shreddable with a fork. Stir occasionally. Add a splash of water or broth if sauce becomes too thick.
Remove bay leaf. Use two forks to shred the lamb directly in the pot. Stir shredded lamb into the sauce.
Cook pappardelle in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and a small sprig of fresh basil or parsley.
notes: For a richer flavor, brown the lamb thoroughly before adding other ingredients.
Adjust the consistency of the ragu by adding a little water or broth if it becomes too thick during simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Lentil Bharwan Shimla Mirch
recipes.visual_description: A single vibrant stuffed bell pepper, such as a bright red one, stands upright as the centerpiece on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone. The pepper is whole, with its top gently placed back on, suggesting a lid. The skin shows a slight char from cooking, indicating tenderness. A small, organic swirl of the earthy-toned bell pepper core chutney is placed to the side, maintaining ample white space on the plate. The filling, visible from the top, is a rustic mix of lentils and finely diced vegetables, showcasing natural colors and textures. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wooden surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin is folded simply beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting textures. The background is minimalist, possibly with a blurred natural plant element, creating an uncluttered, eco-conscious setup.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain, fluffy basmati rice or millet.
Offer a simple cucumber raita (yogurt dip) on the side.
instructions: Soak moong dal for 4-6 hours. Drain. Leave in a warm place for 12-24 hours to lightly ferment. It should develop a slight tang. Rinse lightly before use.
Wash bell peppers. Carefully cut off tops (stems attached) and set aside. Remove and reserve cores and seeds for chutney. Clean inside of peppers.

Heat 15ml oil in a pan. Add chopped onion. Sauté until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and minced green chili. Sauté 1 minute. Add finely diced mixed vegetables. Cook 3-5 minutes until slightly tender.
Add all powdered spices: cumin, coriander, turmeric, red chili, garam masala, asafoetida. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Add lightly fermented moong dal. Mix well.
Cook the dal mixture for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until partially cooked and relatively dry. Stir in fresh coriander and salt. Let cool slightly.
Carefully fill each bell pepper with the dal-vegetable mixture. Do not overstuff. Place the reserved bell pepper tops back on.
Heat 15ml oil in a wide, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven. Carefully place stuffed bell peppers in the pan. Add 100ml water or vegetable stock to the bottom of the pan.
Cover and cook on low heat for 20-25 minutes. Bell peppers should be tender but hold shape. Dal should be fully cooked. Turn occasionally for even cooking.

While peppers cook, make chutney. Heat 5ml oil in a small pan. Add cumin seeds. Once they splutter, add bell pepper cores, stems, seeds, chopped tomato, garlic, ginger, and green chili (if using). Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Let chutney mixture cool. Transfer to a blender. Add salt and tamarind paste (if using). Blend to a smooth paste, adding minimal water if needed.
Carefully transfer one stuffed bell pepper to each plate. Serve with a small dollop or swirl of the bell pepper core chutney on the side.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing bell pepper cores and stems for a flavorful chutney.
Light fermentation of moong dal adds a subtle tang and enhances digestibility.
Adjust spice levels to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Lemon-Mustard Potatoes and Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, deeply golden-brown with crispy skin, rests on a pristine round white porcelain plate. Beside it, a small mound of fluffy saffron-infused Basmati rice, its pale yellow hue contrasting with the vibrant roasted vegetables. Two thick-cut potato wedges, their skins slightly blistered, and a few caramelized red onion wedges and halved cherry tomatoes are artfully arranged near the chicken, showcasing their rich, roasted textures. A light drizzle of pan juices glazes the chicken and vegetables. The dish is garnished with a small sprig of fresh green parsley, adding a pop of color. The plate is centered on a light wooden table surface, accompanied by a simple white linen napkin and polished silver cutlery. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, creating an inviting, casual bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the flavorful pan juices.
A simple green salad with a lemon vinaigrette complements the richness.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine chicken thighs, quartered potatoes, red onion wedges, halved cherry tomatoes, and smashed garlic.
In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, 45ml olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, dried oregano, salt, and pepper.
Pour mustard mixture over chicken and vegetables. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken and vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Pour chicken broth over ingredients on the tray. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender.
While chicken roasts, prepare saffron rice. Steep saffron threads in hot water for 10 minutes.
In a medium saucepan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Add rice and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in 400ml water and saffron liquid. Add a pinch of salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
To serve, plate one chicken thigh, a portion of roasted vegetables, and a scoop of saffron rice.
Drizzle with pan juices. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Mole Poblano
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Pollo en Mole Poblano is presented on a clean, round, white porcelain dinner plate. A large, dark-skinned chicken thigh, deeply caramelized from searing, rests prominently on a pool of rich, glossy mole sauce. The mole, a deep, complex reddish-brown, exhibits a smooth, thick consistency, clinging to the chicken. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped fresh cilantro leaves provides a vibrant color contrast against the dark sauce, along with a sprinkle of pale, toasted sesame seeds for texture. The chicken piece is whole, showcasing its succulent, tender appearance. The plate sits on a simple, warm-toned wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp, folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. A small, white ceramic bowl of fluffy white rice and a stack of warm, soft corn tortillas are positioned nearby, along with a traditional Mexican talavera-style water glass. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the sauce's sheen and the chicken's inviting texture, creating an authentic and approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the mole sauce.
Accompany with a side of traditional Mexican rice.
Offer a small bowl of pickled red onions or jalapeños for a tangy counterpoint.
Serve with a refreshing Agua Fresca or Horchata.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt.
Sear chicken skin-side down in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Cook until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear other side briefly. Remove chicken, set aside.

Carefully remove stems and seeds from dried chiles. Toast chiles in the dry pot for 30 seconds per side until fragrant. Do not burn. Place chiles in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let rehydrate for 20 minutes.
In the same pot, add a little oil. Sauté chopped tomatoes, onion, and garlic until softened and lightly browned.

Drain rehydrated chiles. Add chiles, sautéed vegetables, almonds, raisins, half of the sesame seeds, tortilla piece, cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, and cumin seeds to a blender. Add 200 ml chicken broth.
Blend until very smooth. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Press solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.

Heat 15 ml lard or oil in the pot over medium heat. Add strained mole paste. Cook, stirring constantly, for 10-15 minutes. The paste will thicken and darken. This step is crucial for flavor development.
Gradually whisk in remaining chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add chopped dark chocolate and sugar. Stir until chocolate is fully melted and incorporated. Season with salt to taste.

Return seared chicken thighs to the mole sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Serve chicken with mole sauce. Garnish with fresh cilantro and remaining toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The mole paste requires patient cooking to develop its deep flavor and color.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Parmesan Crusted Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, pan-fried chicken cutlet, approximately 1.5 cm thick, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is generously crusted with toasted parmesan and Panko breadcrumbs, revealing a crisp, textured surface. A vibrant, rich red basil tomato sauce, subtly infused with hot sauce, is spooned beneath and partially over the chicken. The sauce is thick, with visible flecks of diced onion and garlic. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the chicken and sauce. The dish is presented with moderate negative space. A thick slice of golden-toasted garlic bread is placed alongside. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and classic stainless steel flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a side of pasta (e.g., spaghetti or penne) or crusty garlic bread.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.

ingredients.name: Hot sauce (e.g., Calabrian chili paste or cayenne-based)

instructions: Prepare chicken: Slice each chicken breast horizontally into two thinner cutlets. Place cutlets between two sheets of parchment paper. Pound gently with a meat mallet to an even 1.5 cm thickness.

Set up dredging station: Place flour in a shallow dish. In a second shallow dish, whisk eggs. In a third dish, combine grated parmesan and Panko breadcrumbs. Season breadcrumb mix with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Coat chicken: Season chicken cutlets with salt and pepper. Dredge each cutlet first in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, allowing excess to drip off. Finally, press into the parmesan breadcrumb mixture, ensuring a thick, even coating on all sides.

Cook chicken: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Carefully place chicken cutlets in the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Pan-fry for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken and place on a wire rack to drain. Keep warm.

Prepare sauce: In the same skillet, add remaining 20 ml olive oil. Add diced onion and sauté over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in crushed tomatoes, hot sauce, a pinch of sugar (if using), and season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Finish sauce: Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Stir in most of the chopped fresh basil.
Prepare garlic bread: Toast or grill slices of crusty bread. Rub with a cut garlic clove and drizzle with olive oil.

Serve: Spoon a generous amount of spicy basil tomato sauce onto each plate. Place a crispy chicken cutlet on top of the sauce. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately with a side of garlic bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Brown Rice & Swiss Chard Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Savory Brown Rice & Swiss Chard Soup is presented in a clean, matte white porcelain bowl, centrally placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. The soup features a clear, golden-brown broth with vibrant elements. Small, perfectly diced orange carrots and tender, roughly chopped deep green Swiss chard leaves are suspended throughout. Cooked brown rice grains are visible, adding a hearty texture. A delicate swirl of toasted sesame oil glistens on the surface. The soup is garnished generously with thinly sliced bright green scallions and fresh, vibrant cilantro leaves, carefully arranged to add a pop of color and freshness. A crisp, folded white cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. The setting is a modern bistro, illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting from the side, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the fresh ingredients. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distracting from the dish. The entire bowl is visible, showcasing a balanced and appealing composition with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Rinse brown rice. Cook rice according to package directions until tender. Set aside.
Separate Swiss chard leaves from stems. Thinly slice chard stems. Roughly chop chard leaves.
Peel and finely dice carrots into small cubes.
Peel and finely dice onion. Mince garlic. Grate ginger.
Heat 10 ml of toasted sesame oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion and carrots. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add sliced chard stems. Simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in chopped chard leaves. Cook 3-5 minutes until leaves are tender but still vibrant.
Add cooked brown rice to the soup.
Stir in dried oregano and soy sauce. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 5 ml toasted sesame oil.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Turkey Meatloaf with Onion Gravy
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty, thick rectangular slice of golden-brown Homestyle Turkey Meatloaf rests on an everyday off-white ceramic plate. The meatloaf, with its rustic, slightly textured surface, is generously draped with a rich, dark brown onion gravy, showcasing softened, thinly sliced caramelized onions within. A few flecks of fresh green parsley are sprinkled over the gravy. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple silver fork is placed beside the plate. The scene is lit by warm, natural kitchen lighting, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
In a large bowl, combine ground turkey, diced onion, minced garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, milk, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, chopped parsley, dried thyme, salt, and pepper.
Mix ingredients thoroughly but gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into a loaf shape on a baking sheet or in a loaf pan.
Bake for 60-70 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While meatloaf bakes, prepare the gravy. Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add thinly sliced onion to the saucepan. Sauté until softened and caramelized, about 10-15 minutes.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, creating a roux.
Gradually whisk in beef broth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly until gravy thickens.
Season gravy with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove meatloaf from oven. Let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
Slice meatloaf into thick, rectangular portions. Serve hot with onion gravy.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Tofu, Chard & Carrot Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single, comforting portion of Savory Tofu, Chard & Carrot Rice Bowl is presented in an everyday, slightly imperfect, plain ceramic bowl, showcasing its homely appeal. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, inviting kitchen light, suggesting a relaxed family meal. Fluffy, cooked brown rice forms the base, its natural texture visible. Generously piled atop are irregular 2cm golden-brown seared tofu cubes, showing a tender interior. Interspersed are vibrant green, roughly chopped swiss chard leaves, gently wilted, and bright orange carrot batons, thinly cut. The components are casually arranged, naturally overlapping. A subtle drizzle of toasted sesame oil adds a sheen. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed, slightly crumpled cloth napkin, completing the authentic home kitchen scene.
instructions: Cook brown rice. Combine 200g rice with 400ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 40-45 minutes until tender. Let stand 10 minutes.
Press tofu. Cut into 2cm cubes.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add tofu. Sear until golden. Remove from pan.
Wash swiss chard. Separate leaves from stems. Chop stems into 1cm pieces. Roughly chop leaves.
Peel carrots. Cut into thin batons.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the pan. Add chopped chard stems and carrots. Sauté 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped chard leaves to pan. Sauté until wilted, 2-3 minutes.
Return seared tofu to pan. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar, and dried oregano. Stir to combine. Cook 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in toasted sesame oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve cooked brown rice into bowls. Top with the tofu and vegetable mixture.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Baked Chicken with Cheesy Garlic Breadcrumbs
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Spicy Baked Chicken with Cheesy Garlic Breadcrumbs rests on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Two generous, golden-brown baked chicken thighs, each topped with a thick, textured crust of crispy breadcrumbs, melted Parmesan, and flecks of green basil, are nestled in a vibrant reddish-orange tomato sauce. The chicken pieces are whole, un-sliced, with their natural contours. The sauce, visible around the chicken, contains finely diced onion and garlic. A few fresh basil leaves are casually torn and scattered over the dish as garnish. The plate, with its slightly irregular rim, sits on a warm-toned, well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are placed to the side. A crumpled, plain linen napkin and a small, slightly chipped ceramic bowl holding extra grated Parmesan complete the homely setting. Soft, warm light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and rich colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple side of steamed green beans or a light green salad.

ingredients.name: fresh basil leaves
ingredients.quantity: 30g, roughly chopped, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Pulse stale bread in a food processor to make coarse breadcrumbs.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet or large pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, hot sauce, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Place chicken thighs into the simmering sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
In a bowl, combine breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan, and chopped basil.
Spoon the breadcrumb mixture evenly over each chicken thigh in the pan.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake 25-30 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken. It must reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Serve hot.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
For best results, use day-old bread to make fresh breadcrumbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Caramelized Onions and Garlic Herb Butter
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Caramelized Onions and Garlic Herb Butter is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two thick, seared beef medallions, displaying a rich, dark brown crust, are positioned slightly offset in the center of the plate. Adjacent to the beef, a generous portion of deeply golden-brown, glistening caramelized onions, thinly sliced, creates a soft, inviting mound. A glossy, rich brown pan sauce is drizzled artfully over the beef and around the onions. A small, vibrant green sprig of fresh thyme rests gently on top of one beef medallion. The overall composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, under natural, even lighting, conveying a refined yet approachable casual dining atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on all sides. Cut beef into 4 thick medallions (approximately 150g each).
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer to desired doneness. Do not overcrowd the pan. Sear in batches if necessary.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 30g butter, 2 thyme sprigs, and 1 rosemary sprig to the skillet. Tilt the pan and spoon melted butter over beef for 1-2 minutes.
Remove beef from skillet. Place on a cutting board, tent with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.
In the same skillet, add thinly sliced onions. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender. Add a splash of water if onions stick.
Add minced garlic to onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook until sauce slightly reduces and thickens, about 5 minutes. Stir in remaining 30g butter and chopped parsley. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Plate beef medallions. Spoon caramelized onions next to or over beef. Drizzle with pan sauce. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Potato and Tomato Curry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Spicy Potato and Tomato Curry is presented in a deep, white ceramic bowl. The curry showcases medium 2cm potato cubes and softened tomato pieces, coated in a rich, reddish-orange sauce. The surface shimmers slightly, indicating a well-cooked, flavorful base. A generous scattering of bright green, freshly chopped coriander leaves provides a striking color contrast and fresh texture. The dish is centrally placed on a simple wooden table, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Beside the bowl, a small portion of fluffy Basmati rice is neatly arranged, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a clean, inviting atmosphere. The plating is professional and approachable, with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish as the main subject.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with freshly cooked Basmati rice.
Serve with warm naan bread or roti for scooping the curry.
instructions: Heat oil or ghee in a large pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds. Cook until they splutter, about 30 seconds.
Add chopped onions. Sauté until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, cayenne pepper, turmeric powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down and oil separates from the mixture.
Add diced potatoes. Stir to coat them thoroughly with the spice mixture.
Pour in water or vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Stir in garam masala. Cook for 2 minutes uncovered.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. The curry should have a medium-thick consistency.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander before serving.
notes: Adjust cayenne pepper to your preferred spice level.
For a richer flavor, use ghee instead of vegetable oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Carnitas with Arroz Rojo and Esquites
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pork Carnitas is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The savory, golden-brown, crispy pork chunks are piled centrally. Beside the pork is a portion of vibrant red Arroz Rojo, fluffy and speckled with tomato. Adjacent to the rice, a mound of Esquites, featuring charred corn kernels mixed with creamy mayonnaise and crumbled Cotija cheese, adds a contrasting texture and color. A fresh lime wedge rests on the side. The plate is set on a simple wooden table. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The background is a softly blurred modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the ingredients, emphasizing the authentic Mexican flavors. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced and appealing composition with appropriate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for making tacos.
Offer various salsas (salsa verde, pico de gallo) on the side.
Provide extra lime wedges and chopped cilantro for garnish.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5 cm chunks. Pat dry.
Place pork chunks in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven. Add lard, orange halves, onion, garlic, bay leaves, and salt.
Pour in water. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2-3 hours. Pork should be very tender.
Remove lid. Increase heat to medium-high. Cook until liquid evaporates and pork begins to crisp and brown in the rendered lard. Stir occasionally. Cook until internal temperature reaches 63°C.
Remove pork from lard. Shred or chop into smaller pieces. Set aside.
For Arroz Rojo: Rinse rice under cold water until clear. Drain well.
Heat a splash of oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add rice. Cook, stirring, until lightly toasted, about 5 minutes.
Add diced tomato. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
For Esquites: Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Add corn kernels. Cook, stirring frequently, until lightly charred, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove corn from heat. Transfer to a bowl. Stir in mayonnaise, half of the Cotija cheese, chili powder, and half of the cilantro. Mix well.
Warm tortillas on a griddle or in a microwave.
Serve crispy pork carnitas with a side of Arroz Rojo and Esquites. Garnish with remaining Cotija cheese, cilantro, and lime wedges.
notes: Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) for safe consumption, then allow to rest for 3 minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Lamb Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of golden pappardelle pasta is gently coiled on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate, forming an inviting mound. The pasta is richly coated in a deep reddish-brown lamb ragu, showcasing tender, pulled lamb chunks and dark, sautéed mushroom slices. The ragu's texture is thick and rustic, clinging to the wide pasta ribbons. Bright green specks of fresh, chopped rosemary and parsley are scattered over the dish, adding a vibrant contrast. A fine dusting of grated Parmesan cheese lightly crowns the top. The lamb is presented as robust, shredded pieces integrated into the sauce. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a clean white cotton napkin and classic flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its warm colors and inviting textures. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
A glass of robust red wine
instructions: Season lamb cubes with salt and pepper. Dice lamb into 2-3 cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb in batches until browned on all sides. Remove lamb and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped rosemary. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until softened and lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Deglaze pot with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return seared lamb to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and beef broth.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2-3 hours until lamb is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove lamb from pot. Shred lamb using two forks. Return shredded lamb to the sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Cook pappardelle according to package instructions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving some pasta water.
Add cooked pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to combine, adding a splash of reserved pasta water if needed.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken with Fermented Tomato Essence
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly slow-cooked chicken thigh sits centrally on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The chicken, presented whole with its bone, features a beautifully crisped, golden-brown skin. Beside it, a rich, deep red-orange pool of reduced fermented tomato essence gleams. Scattered around the chicken are a few whole, roasted garlic cloves, their skins lightly charred, revealing soft, creamy interiors. A small, artfully arranged cluster of vibrant green seasonal vegetables adds a fresh counterpoint. The composition emphasizes natural shapes and textures, with ample white space on the plate. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, diffused natural light from the side, creating a clean, minimalist, and eco-conscious aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Seasonal green vegetables (e.g., asparagus, green beans)

instructions: Chop tomatoes into quarters. Place in a clean 1.5-litre glass jar.
Dissolve 20g sea salt in 1 litre filtered water to make a brine. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight to keep tomatoes under liquid.
Seal jar loosely. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Bubbles indicate active fermentation. Strain fermented tomatoes. Reserve liquid (fermented tomato essence).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Carefully remove skin from thighs. Set skin aside. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, flesh side down, for 4-5 minutes until golden brown. Flip. Sear skin side down for 2-3 minutes.
Pour reserved fermented tomato essence over chicken. Add unpeeled garlic cloves from the whole head.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C.
Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and internal temperature reaches 75°C.

While chicken braises, place reserved chicken skin in a cold, dry pan. Heat over medium-low heat. Slowly render fat and crisp skin, pressing down occasionally, until deeply golden and shatteringly crisp (10-15 minutes). Remove from pan. Drain on paper towel. Season with a pinch of salt.
Remove chicken from pot. Set aside. Strain braising liquid into a small saucepan, discarding garlic skins if desired. Keep roasted garlic cloves.
Bring liquid to a vigorous simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce until thickened to a desired sauce consistency (approx. 5-10 minutes).
Blanch or steam green vegetables until tender-crisp.

Place one slow-cooked chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon reduced fermented tomato essence around chicken. Arrange a few roasted garlic cloves and a small portion of green vegetables beside chicken. Crumble crisped chicken skin over or beside the chicken. Serve immediately.
notes: Chicken bones can be saved for making stock.
Fermented tomato pulp can be used in other dishes, such as a base for soup or a spread.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Rice Cake with Poached Egg, Tomato Confit, and Noodle Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown seared rice cake sits off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. A perfectly poached egg, its delicate white encasing a visible yolk, rests atop or beside it. Around the base, glossy, ruby-red confit cherry tomatoes, some slightly burst, gleam with their rich oil. Vibrant emerald-green green onion oil is artfully drizzled, creating subtle pools that contrast with the porcelain. A small, airy cluster of golden crispy noodles is delicately perched, adding textural counterpoint. The minimalist composition features generous negative space, emphasizing precise component placement. The scene is on a luxurious grey-veined marble surface, with dramatic professional lighting and soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded precisely, completes the elegant background.

ingredients.name: green onion (white and light green parts), thinly sliced

instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C. Place cherry tomatoes, olive oil, sliced garlic, thyme, salt, and sugar in a small oven-safe dish. Toss gently. Roast for 45-60 minutes, or until tomatoes are soft and slightly shriveled. Remove thyme sprig. Set aside.

Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add sliced green onion. Gently simmer for 15-20 minutes, until green onions are fragrant and slightly crisp. Strain oil through a fine-mesh sieve into a heatproof bowl. Discard solids. Stir in sesame oil and salt. Set aside.

In a bowl, combine cooked sushi rice, rice flour, sesame oil, and salt. Mix thoroughly by hand until well combined and slightly sticky. Form into 4 compact, flat discs, about 1.5 cm thick and 6-7 cm in diameter.

Heat neutral oil in a small pot to 175°C. Carefully add a small handful of egg noodles. Fry for 10-20 seconds until golden and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt. Repeat with remaining noodles.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of neutral oil. Carefully place rice cakes in the pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.

Bring a large pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add white vinegar. Carefully crack each egg into a separate small bowl. Gently slide eggs into simmering water. Cook for 3-4 minutes for a runny yolk. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain excess water.

Place one seared rice cake slightly off-center on each plate. Gently place a poached egg on top of or slightly next to the rice cake. Spoon a few confit cherry tomatoes and a drizzle of their oil around the rice cake. Drizzle generously with green onion oil. Garnish with a small, delicate cluster of crispy noodles.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of baked chicken with roasted vegetables rests on an off-white ceramic dinner plate. A golden-brown, tender chicken thigh is positioned slightly off-center. Around the chicken, a natural scattering of vibrant green broccoli florets, deep brown sliced mushrooms, soft reddish-brown onion wedges, and burst red cherry tomatoes creates a comforting, abundant feel. Some vegetables display slight charring on their edges, indicating the roasting process. A light sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the dish. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a modest, homely portion. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting. A simple fork and knife are placed beside the plate on a casual paper towel, reflecting an everyday family meal atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place broccoli florets, sliced mushrooms, onion wedges, and halved cherry tomatoes into a large mixing bowl.
Add olive oil, minced garlic, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper to the vegetables. Toss until vegetables are evenly coated.
Spread the seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken with additional salt and pepper.
Arrange chicken thighs among the vegetables on the baking sheet.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. Chicken is done when internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Coconut Chicken Soup (Tom Kha Gai)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Thai Coconut Chicken Soup (Tom Kha Gai) is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The soup, a milky white from the coconut milk, has visible chunks of cooked white chicken and light brown, tender sliced oyster mushrooms. Bright green pieces of chopped cilantro are scattered over the top, with a few vibrant red chili slices adding a pop of color. The surface of the soup shows subtle steam rising. The bowl sits on a simple, light wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro setting. To the side, a traditional white ceramic Chinese soup spoon rests on the table. A small, neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, maintaining focus on the elegantly plated soup. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting, highlighting the fresh ingredients and the soup's comforting warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side bowl of steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a small dish of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies) for individual seasoning adjustment.
instructions: Slice chicken breast into 2 cm thick chunks. Set aside.
Thinly slice galangal. Smash lemongrass stalks with the back of a knife; cut into 5 cm pieces. Tear kaffir lime leaves.
In a medium pot, combine chicken broth, galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add chicken chunks to the simmering broth. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Skim any foam.
Add coconut milk and sliced oyster mushrooms. Bring to a gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously after adding coconut milk.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed for a balance of sour, salty, and sweet.
Thinly slice red chilies. Roughly chop cilantro.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh cilantro and sliced red chilies. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Infusion of aromatics (galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves)
Balancing of four key flavors: sour, salty, sweet, and spicy

recipes.recipe_name: Penne al Pomodoro Arrosto con Burrata
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of penne pasta is artfully arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing its vibrant roasted tomato sauce. The pasta is tossed with a rich, reddish-orange sauce, highlighting the softened, blistered roasted cherry tomatoes, some whole and some gently burst, alongside golden-brown, tender whole garlic cloves. Fresh green basil leaves are generously scattered throughout, providing a striking color contrast. A generous dollop of creamy white burrata is torn and placed gently atop the pasta, its soft interior beginning to melt into the warm sauce. The dish is presented with moderate negative space, allowing each ingredient to be appreciated. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin and a polished fork and spoon are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating an inviting, authentic Italian dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano
Crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place cherry tomatoes and whole garlic cloves on a baking tray. Drizzle with 50 ml olive oil. Season with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using).
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tomatoes are blistered and garlic is tender.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add penne pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, transfer roasted tomatoes and garlic to a large pan. Gently mash some tomatoes to create a rustic sauce. Add remaining 50 ml olive oil.
Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml of pasta water.
Add drained pasta to the pan with the roasted tomato sauce. Add half of the fresh basil leaves, torn.
Toss well, adding reserved pasta water as needed to create a light sauce consistency.
Tear burrata into large pieces. Gently fold into the pasta or place on top when serving.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork and Mushrooms
recipes.special_requests: 中国菜 cuisine, 不用烤箱
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Braised Pork and Mushrooms is presented in a deep, simple white ceramic bowl, characteristic of everyday Chinese home dining. The pork, cut into robust 3cm chunks, is fork-tender and retains its natural browned exterior from searing, contrasting with the soft, pale interior. Thickly sliced button mushrooms are interspersed among the pork, their earthy brown caps peeking through. The dish is coated in a rich, opaque white sauce, naturally thickened to a silky consistency, which pools gently around the ingredients. The sauce has a subtle sheen, inviting warmth. A sprinkle of bright green chopped spring onion is scattered over the top, providing a fresh color contrast. The bowl is placed on a well-worn, light wooden kitchen table, slightly scuffed from family use. Beside it, a small, individual serving of fluffy white steamed rice sits in a traditional Chinese rice bowl. A pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests beside the rice bowl. The setting is casually arranged, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting, suggesting a comforting family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
Offer a side of blanched green vegetables like gai lan or bok choy.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 3cm chunks.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large pot over medium-high heat.
Add pork chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove pork.
Add minced garlic, ginger slices, and white parts of spring onions to the wok. Stir-fry until fragrant.
Return pork to the wok. Add Shaoxing wine and light soy sauce. Stir well.
Pour in chicken or pork broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 45-60 minutes, or until pork is tender.
Add thickly sliced mushrooms to the pot. Cook for 10-15 minutes, until mushrooms are tender.
Stir the cornstarch slurry. Slowly pour into the simmering sauce, stirring constantly until sauce thickens to a milky, opaque consistency.
Season with white pepper and salt to taste.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Garnish with green parts of spring onions.
Ensure internal temperature of pork reaches 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Tomato Noodles with Scrambled Egg
recipes.visual_description: The Garlic Tomato Noodles are presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, showcasing a vibrant medley of colors and textures. Steamed wheat noodles, coated in a light, glossy tomato-garlic sauce, form the base. Interspersed throughout are soft, golden scrambled egg pieces and bright red 1.5 cm diced tomato cubes, some slightly softened, others retaining a hint of firmness. Thinly sliced bright green green onion batons are scattered generously over the top, providing a fresh contrast. A subtle sheen of sesame oil glistens on the noodles. The dish has a natural, flowing arrangement, not overly geometric, with moderate negative space around the edges of the bowl. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the ingredients' fresh appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of plain white rice on the side.
Offer a side of chili oil for those who prefer more heat.
Serve family-style with individual bowls for self-serving.
instructions: Boil noodles according to package instructions until al dente. Drain. Rinse with cold water. Toss with 10 mL sesame oil to prevent sticking.
Whisk eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper. Heat 15 mL vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over medium-high heat. Pour in eggs. Scramble until just set but still moist. Remove from pan. Set aside.
Dice tomatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Mince garlic. Chop green onions, separating white and green parts.
Add remaining 15 mL vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic and white parts of green onions. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes to the wok. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften slightly and release juices.
Stir in soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Add drained noodles to the wok. Toss well to coat noodles evenly with sauce and tomato mixture. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing noodles to absorb flavors.
Return scrambled eggs to the wok. Gently fold into the noodles.
Remove from heat. Drizzle with remaining 20 mL sesame oil. Garnish with green parts of green onions. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust soy sauce and sugar to taste based on tomato sweetness.
For an extra layer of flavor, consider adding a dash of white pepper or a pinch of five-spice powder to the sauce.
Ensure noodles are not overcooked to maintain their texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Herb Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous, single portion of creamy garlic herb chicken and mushroom pasta is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The pasta, a mix of penne and fettuccine, is generously coated in a rich, velvety cream sauce. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks are interspersed throughout the pasta, alongside earthy, sautéed mushroom slices. Fresh, vibrant green parsley is sprinkled over the top, adding a pop of color. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese provides a subtle white contrast. The dish is arranged naturally, with ingredients overlapping and touching, creating a comforting, inviting pile. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A casual, folded linen napkin and a fork rest beside the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty garlic bread.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette.
instructions: Cut chicken into 2.5 cm cubes. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic. Dice onion.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through. Remove chicken from pan.
Add butter to the pan. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Return cooked chicken to the pan. Add cooked pasta. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Potato Bake with Mozzarella and Basil Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the Rustic Chicken and Potato Bake is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, showcasing a harmonious blend of textures and colors. Golden-brown seared chicken thigh pieces are nestled among tender, slightly caramelized potato chunks and vibrant, burst cherry tomatoes. Melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese generously drapes over the ingredients. A scoop of fluffy, green-flecked basil rice is neatly plated beside the baked components. Fresh basil leaves are scattered artfully over both the chicken bake and the rice, adding a pop of fresh green. The dish is set on a simple wooden table with natural, even lighting. A crisp white linen napkin and standard cutlery are placed beside the plate, completing a refined yet approachable bistro setting. A small, rustic bowl of grated Parmesan cheese is placed nearby for cultural authenticity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for soaking up juices.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper, and 2g oregano.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Slice onion into thick wedges. Halve cherry tomatoes. Mince garlic.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the skillet. Add potatoes and onion. Sauté 5 minutes until lightly softened. Add minced garlic and remaining 3g oregano. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared chicken to the skillet with potatoes and onion. Add cherry tomatoes and corn. Toss gently to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Bake for 20 minutes. Internal temperature of chicken should reach 75°C.

While bake cooks, prepare basil rice. Rinse rice under cold water. In a medium saucepan, combine rice and chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15-18 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Chop fresh basil. Stir half of the chopped basil into the cooked rice. Keep warm.
Remove skillet from oven. Tear fresh mozzarella into pieces. Scatter mozzarella over the chicken and vegetables.
Return to oven for 5-7 minutes, or until mozzarella is melted and bubbly.
Serve baked chicken and vegetables immediately with a side of basil rice. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Home-Style Pork Stir-fry
recipes.special_requests: 中国菜 cuisine, 不用烤箱
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest serving of Spicy Home-Style Pork Stir-fry is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a subtle blue-grey rim, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features natural, irregular thin slices of stir-fried pork belly, glistening with a dark, savory sauce. The pork is mixed with vibrant green chili pieces, some showing slight charring from the high heat cooking. Thinly sliced garlic and ginger are visible, adding texture and aroma. The components are casually arranged, overlapping slightly, filling the plate without overcrowding. Next to the main dish, a small, white ceramic rice bowl filled with fluffy steamed white rice sits. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests casually beside the rice bowl. A simple, casually folded beige cloth napkin is nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, natural light, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with hot steamed white rice.
Best enjoyed family-style, with multiple dishes shared among diners.

ingredients.name: Green chilies (e.g., Anaheim or long green peppers)

instructions: Slice pork belly or shoulder into thin, bite-sized pieces (about 0.5 cm thick).
In a bowl, marinate pork with 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, 0.5 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, white pepper, and cornstarch. Mix well. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Slice green chilies diagonally into 2 cm pieces.
Slice garlic and ginger thinly.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until smoking. Add 1 tablespoon vegetable oil.
Add marinated pork to the wok. Stir-fry until browned and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes. Remove pork from wok and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil to the wok. Add sliced garlic and ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced green chilies to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened but still crisp.
Return cooked pork to the wok.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, 0.5 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, and sugar. Stir well to combine all ingredients.
Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until everything is well coated and heated through. Taste and adjust salt if needed.
Serve immediately with steamed white rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Simple Roasted Lamb with Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Simple Roasted Lamb with Vegetables is presented on an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic plate with earthy tones. The dish features golden-brown, tender roasted lamb chunks, approximately 4-5 cm in size, nestled among large, rustic potato wedges, softened red and green bell pepper chunks, and caramelized onion wedges. Smashed garlic cloves are visible throughout. The overall color palette is warm and natural, with rich browns, vibrant reds, and greens. A generous scattering of bright green, fresh chopped parsley provides a final visual lift. The components are arranged naturally, touching and overlapping, reflecting a homely, casual plating style. The plate is adequately filled but not overcrowded, leaving some negative space. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, with warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures. A simple, folded cloth napkin rests casually beside the plate. A small, white ceramic bowl of plain yogurt is placed nearby, along with torn pieces of warm lavash bread in a rustic basket, enhancing the authentic Turkish dining experience. The background shows a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere with minimal, natural clutter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm lavash or pide bread for scooping.
Offer a side of plain yogurt or cacık (cucumber and yogurt dip).
Pair with a simple Shepherd's Salad (Çoban Salatası) of finely diced tomatoes, cucumbers, and onions.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut lamb into 4-5 cm thick chunks. Pat dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine 45 ml olive oil, Dijon mustard, finely chopped rosemary leaves, salt, black pepper, dried oregano, and red pepper flakes. Mix well.
Add lamb chunks to the bowl. Toss to coat evenly. Let marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Cut potatoes, bell peppers, and onion into large, rustic chunks. Smash garlic cloves.
Add cut vegetables and smashed garlic to the lamb in the bowl. Add tomato paste and remaining 15 ml olive oil. Toss everything together to combine.
Transfer the lamb and vegetable mixture to a large roasting pan. Spread in a single layer.
Pour water or broth into the bottom of the roasting pan.
Roast for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lamb is tender and vegetables are browned and cooked through. Ensure lamb reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve hot. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This recipe is designed for ease and comfort, using basic kitchen equipment.
Marinating the lamb for longer, even overnight in the refrigerator, will enhance flavor and tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Chili Verde
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Pork Chili Verde is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. Tender, shredded pork chunks are nestled within a vibrant, rich green sauce. The sauce has a natural, slightly textured appearance from the blended tomatillos and chilies, clinging well to the pork. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green cilantro is casually scattered over the top. The bowl sits on a well-worn, light wooden kitchen table, indicating a homely family setting. Next to the bowl, a stack of warm, soft corn tortillas is wrapped in a simple, off-white cloth napkin. A small ceramic plate holds a few extra lime wedges and a scattering of fresh cilantro leaves, ready for customization. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting light, suggesting a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, focusing on the hearty, comforting essence of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer crumbled queso fresco or Mexican crema as toppings.
Provide extra lime wedges and fresh cilantro for garnish.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 4-5 cm thick chunks. Season generously with salt.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot. Set aside.
Remove husks from tomatillos. Rinse well. Cut tomatillos in half.
Stem serrano chilies. Roughly chop onion and garlic.
Add tomatillos, serrano chilies, onion, and garlic to the same pot. Cook for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly charred. Stir occasionally.
Transfer cooked vegetables and chilies to a blender. Add 120 ml chicken broth, cumin, and oregano. Blend until smooth.
Pour the blended sauce back into the pot. Add remaining chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared pork chunks to the pot. Ensure pork is mostly submerged in sauce. If not, add a little more broth or water.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot. Simmer for 2-3 hours, or until pork is very tender and easily shreds with a fork.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Add more liquid if sauce becomes too thick.
Remove pork from pot. Shred pork chunks into smaller pieces using two forks. Return shredded pork to the sauce.
Stir in freshly chopped cilantro. Taste and adjust salt as needed.
Serve hot.
notes: Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of at least 70°C (158°F) for tenderness, though it will cook much higher during the long braise.
For spicier chili verde, include the seeds from the serrano chilies. For milder, remove seeds or use fewer chilies.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Korean Beef and Pork Jeongol
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, steaming Korean hot pot (Jeongol) presented in a wide, shallow, dark-colored ceramic or cast-iron pot. The thinly sliced, marinated beef and pork are arranged artfully over a bed of napa cabbage, shiitake mushrooms, and tofu rectangles. Bright red gochujang-based broth bubbles gently around the ingredients. Slices of onion and long segments of green onion add contrast. Cooked dangmyeon noodles and delicate enoki mushrooms are nestled among the meats and vegetables. The dish is garnished with fresh, vibrant green scallion batons. The pot sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by small white porcelain bowls of steamed white rice and a few traditional Korean banchan (side dishes like kimchi and pickled radishes) in small, simple ceramic dishes. A set of metal chopsticks rests beside a clean white porcelain serving bowl, ready for individual portions. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and rich colors of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve communally directly from the hot pot.
Provide individual bowls of steamed white rice.
Offer a selection of banchan (small side dishes) such as kimchi, pickled radishes, and seasoned spinach.
Use metal chopsticks and a deep spoon for serving broth.

ingredients.name: Thinly sliced beef brisket or sirloin
Thinly sliced pork belly or shoulder
Napa cabbage, cut into large pieces
Firm tofu, sliced into 1 cm thick rectangles
Green onions, cut into 5 cm lengths

instructions: Prepare marinade: Combine minced garlic, grated ginger, gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sesame oil, mirin, sugar, and black pepper in a large bowl.
Marinate meat: Add thinly sliced beef and pork to the marinade. Mix well. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.

Prepare vegetables: Cut napa cabbage into large pieces. Slice shiitake mushrooms. Separate enoki mushrooms. Slice tofu. Slice onion. Cut green onions. Soak dangmyeon in warm water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Assemble hot pot: Arrange napa cabbage, sliced onion, shiitake mushrooms, and tofu in the bottom of a wide, shallow pot (jeongol pot or similar).
Add meat: Place marinated beef and pork slices attractively on top of the vegetables.
Add broth: Pour beef broth or water into the pot.
Cook: Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until meats are cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Add noodles and enoki: Add soaked dangmyeon and enoki mushrooms during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Garnish: Sprinkle with fresh green onions just before serving.
Serve: Serve hot directly from the pot, with individual bowls of rice and banchan.
notes: Adjust gochugaru for desired spice level.
Skim any foam from the broth during cooking for a clearer soup.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Mushroom & Black Bean 'Chorizo' with Red Rice and Fermented Tomatillo Salsa
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a rustic yet refined single portion on a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic plate. At the center, a generous mound of vibrant red rice, each grain distinct, offers a soft, earthy base. Adjacent, substantial chunks of smoky mushroom and black bean 'chorizo' are artfully arranged, showcasing their rich, dark brown color and textural crumble. Scattered around the plate are roasted root vegetable wedges – golden sweet potato, orange carrot – with slightly caramelized edges, glistening from their agave glaze. A bright green fermented tomatillo salsa is spooned alongside, its fresh hue providing a striking contrast. The entire composition is garnished sparingly with fresh cilantro leaves and a bright lime wedge. The plate sits on a light bamboo table surface, accompanied by a natural undyed linen napkin and traditional flatware, and soft, diffused natural lighting illuminates the scene from the side, enhancing the dish's natural colors and textures. No overcrowding, ample white space emphasizes the sustainable ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer additional lime wedges for squeezing over the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel sweet potatoes and carrots. Cut into 2cm wedges and chunks. Reserve peels for broth.
Toss sweet potato and carrot pieces with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp agave nectar, 1 tbsp lime juice, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Flip halfway.
While vegetables roast, prepare the 'chorizo'. Finely dice mushrooms, including stems. Mash rinsed black beans.
Finely dice red onion. Mince garlic. Mince chipotle peppers.
Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in mashed black beans, minced chipotle, adobo sauce, smoked paprika, ground cumin, and dried Mexican oregano. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Rinse brown rice. In a medium saucepan, combine rice, 500ml vegetable broth, and 2 tbsp tomato paste. Add 0.5 tsp salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand covered for 5 minutes.
Prepare the fermented tomatillo salsa. Husk and rinse tomatillos. Roughly chop tomatillos, 1 small onion, and serrano peppers. Mince 1 clove garlic.
Combine chopped tomatillos, onion, serrano peppers, garlic, 0.5 tsp salt, and 0.25 cup water in a blender. Blend until smooth. Add chipotle powder if desired.
Pour salsa into a clean glass jar. Loosely cover. Let ferment at room temperature for 1-2 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermenting.

To serve, spoon a mound of red rice onto each plate. Arrange 'chorizo' chunks alongside the rice. Place roasted root vegetable wedges around. Spoon fermented tomatillo salsa generously over the dish. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and a lime wedge. Serve immediately.
notes: Utilize root vegetable peels and mushroom stems for making vegetable broth to minimize food waste.
The salsa fermentation time can be extended for a deeper, more complex flavor profile. Ensure proper hygiene during fermentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Pork and Bean Chili
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of chili fills a deep, sturdy ceramic bowl, its rich reddish-brown hue indicating robust flavor. The chili is thick and chunky, with visible pieces of browned pork, soft kidney and black beans, and diced tomatoes in a savory sauce. A generous layer of melted shredded yellow cheddar cheese blankets the top, slightly bubbling. A dollop of cool white sour cream sits off-center, its smooth texture contrasting. A sprinkle of bright green, thinly sliced spring onions adds fresh color. The bowl rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden kitchen table, bathed in soft, natural light. A simple metal spoon is tucked into the side. A small piece of golden cornbread is casually placed nearby, completing this quintessential homely comfort meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with shredded cheddar cheese, sour cream, and chopped green onions.
Offer cornbread, crackers, or tortilla chips on the side.
Enjoy as a comforting family meal.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add ground pork. Cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chili powder, ground cumin, dried oregano, and smoked paprika. Stir and cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
Pour in diced tomatoes, kidney beans, black beans, and beef broth. Stir well.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for at least 30 minutes, or up to 1 hour, stirring occasionally. The longer it simmers, the richer the flavor.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot.
notes: For extra heat, add a diced jalapeño or a pinch of cayenne pepper with the other spices.
Chili tastes even better the next day; store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
This chili freezes well for future meals.

recipes.recipe_name: Kuzu Yahni (Turkish Lamb Stew)
recipes.visual_description: A single, inviting portion of Kuzu Yahni is artfully presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Succulent, tender chunks of braised lamb, approximately 3-4 cm cubes, are nestled amidst a rich, deep reddish-brown tomato and onion-based sauce. The lamb exhibits a slight char from initial searing, providing textural contrast. Visible elements include softened onion wedges and vibrant green specks of finely chopped fresh parsley, scattered generously over the top. The stew has a comforting, slightly glossy sheen. A few small, fresh rosemary sprigs are subtly placed for aromatic accent. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish is photographed in a modern bistro setting, on a simple wooden table, with natural, even lighting. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate, accompanied by standard European flatware. The presentation is professional and approachable, highlighting the dish's hearty appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Pirinç Pilavı (Turkish Rice Pilaf) or Bulgur Pilavı (Bulgur Pilaf).
Offer a side of plain yogurt or Çoban Salatasu (Shepherd's Salad).
Provide fresh Turkish bread (ekmek) for dipping into the sauce.
instructions: Cut lamb into 3-4 cm cubes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove lamb from pot.
Add onion wedges to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, tomato paste, pul biber, and cumin. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return lamb to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, lamb broth, and rosemary sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until lamb is very tender.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Stir in most of the fresh parsley. Reserve some for garnish.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality lamb and let the stew simmer slowly.
The rosemary provides a subtle aromatic note, complementing the traditional Turkish spices.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Serve the risotto on a flat white porcelain dinner plate. The consistency is fluid and spreads naturally across the plate, appearing free-flowing rather than molded. The rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, creamy sauce. Large 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are distributed throughout the rice. Sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms show deep caramelization and earthy brown tones. The dish features a pale golden hue. Finely minced flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the surface. The arrangement is organic. Beside the plate sits a heavy silver spoon and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the consistency remains fluid
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Dice onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until moisture evaporates and edges brown.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the pan. Add onion and garlic.
Cook until softened but not browned.
Add rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast the grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Add 200ml warm stock. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Repeat stock additions one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is tender but firm.
Return chicken and mushrooms to the pan.
Remove from heat.
Vigorously stir in remaining 30g butter and Parmesan cheese to create a creamy emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper. Fold in chopped parsley.
notes: Keep the chicken stock at a low simmer in a separate pot to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is essential to release rice starches for a creamy texture.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C during the initial searing phase.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple and Honey Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Apple and Honey Crumble is served in a warm, cream-colored ceramic bowl with slight imperfections, placed on a well-worn wooden dining table. The golden-brown, rustic crumble topping, made from oats and flour, is unevenly scattered over the tender, diced apples. The apples, softened and slightly caramelized from baking with honey and cinnamon, bubble gently beneath the topping, showing warm, golden hues. A small scoop of melting vanilla ice cream rests on the side of the crumble, slightly softening into the warm dessert. The scene is bathed in a soft, warm light, evoking a cozy, lived-in kitchen atmosphere. A simple, everyday spoon rests beside the bowl.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Peel, core, and dice apples into 2 cm cubes.
In a large bowl, toss diced apples with honey and ground cinnamon.
Spread apple mixture evenly into a 20x20 cm baking dish.
In a separate bowl, combine plain flour, rolled oats, light brown sugar, and salt.
Add cold, cubed unsalted butter to the dry ingredients.
Use your fingertips or a pastry blender to cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Sprinkle the crumble topping evenly over the apples in the baking dish.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the apple filling is bubbly and tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Dhania Paneer Masala
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant green Dhania Paneer Masala is served in a deep white porcelain bowl, centrally placed on a light wooden table. The curry is rich and creamy, showcasing a deep, natural green hue from fresh coriander. Approximately six to eight 2cm golden-brown pan-seared paneer cubes are nestled within. A generous swirl of thick white Greek yogurt is artfully drizzled over the top, creating a beautiful contrast. A few fresh coriander sprigs are delicately placed as a garnish. Beside the bowl, a small mound of fluffy basmati rice and a piece of freshly baked naan bread are present. The background is a soft, blurred restaurant setting with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm Basmati rice.
Accompany with fresh naan, roti, or chapati.
Offer a side of cooling raita or pickled onions.
instructions: Cut paneer into 2 cm cubes. Lightly pan-sear paneer until golden. Set aside.
In a blender, combine fresh coriander leaves, green chillies, ginger, and garlic. Add a splash of water. Blend to a smooth paste.
Heat ghee in a large pan over medium heat. Add finely diced onions. Sauté until translucent.
Add tomato puree. Cook until oil separates from the mixture.
Stir in turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and red chilli powder. Cook spices for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the coriander-chilli paste. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring frequently, until the raw aroma disappears.
Add 250 ml hot water. Bring the gravy to a simmer.
Add seared paneer cubes to the simmering gravy. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in garam masala and salt to taste. Cook until the internal temperature of paneer reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Swirl in 50g of Greek yogurt.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot.
notes: Adjust the number of green chillies to control the spice level.
For best flavor, allow the curry to rest for a few minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Frango Assado com Batatas e Cebolas
recipes.visual_description: A single bone-in, skin-on roasted chicken thigh is placed prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken skin is deep golden-brown and visibly crispy, seasoned with herbs and spices. Surrounding the chicken, roasted potato quarters exhibit tender interiors with slightly browned, crisp edges. Caramelized onion wedges, soft and translucent, are scattered among the potatoes. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley is scattered over the entire dish, providing a fresh contrast. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. Beside the plate, a neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware (fork and knife) are present. In the background, slightly out of focus, small white ceramic bowls hold portions of fluffy white rice and golden farofa. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The overall presentation is inviting, warm, and casually elegant, reminiscent of a Brazilian home-style meal served in a modern bistro.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with white rice (arroz branco).
Serve with toasted cassava flour (farofa).
A simple green salad (salada verde) is a common accompaniment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Place in a large bowl.
Mince garlic. Juice the lime. Add minced garlic, lime juice, 30ml olive oil, paprika, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper to chicken.
Mix well. Ensure chicken is fully coated. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours refrigerated.
Scrub potatoes. Quarter them. Cut onions into thick wedges.
In a separate large bowl, combine quartered potatoes and onion wedges.
Drizzle with remaining 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange chicken pieces in a single layer in a large roasting pan.
Scatter potatoes and onions around chicken in the pan.
Roast for 45-60 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Turn potatoes and onions halfway through roasting.
Chicken skin should be golden and crispy. Potatoes should be tender and lightly browned.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish generously with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Marinating the chicken for a longer period enhances its flavor significantly.
Adjust salt and pepper to personal taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli and Tomato Frittata
recipes.visual_description: The Broccoli and Tomato Frittata is presented as a generous, rustic wedge on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The frittata, with a golden-brown top from baking, reveals a dense, fluffy interior studded with vibrant green broccoli florets and bright red halved cherry tomatoes. Thinly sliced, tender, lightly caramelized onions are interspersed throughout the egg base. The broccoli florets are tender-crisp, and the tomatoes retain their shape, adding pops of color.
